English: Fishing Dock
A simple timber platform and shacks for local fishermen, with drying racks and makeshift nets.
Boat Slip
A small sheltered landing for boats, reinforced with logs and earthworks, and a communal shed for storing gear.
Harbormasters Hut
A modest but permanent building for the harbormaster, overseeing docking rights, levying tolls, and managing basic port records.
Pier Wharf
A timber pier juts into the water, allowing several fishing vessels to dock simultaneously. The area bustles with baskets and barrels.
Cargo Jetty
Sturdy stone pilings and a wider dock allow for heavier cargo and merchant vessels to land. Simple cranes and guard posts are present.
Seafarers Wharf
A broad wharf with stone breakwaters, ship chandlers, and secure bonded warehouses. Caravans and coastal traders crowd the bustling scene.
Small Quay
A stone quay with mooring posts and defensive fencing, enabling secure loading and unloading of multiple merchant ships.
Merchant Harbor
A bustling center with warehouses, customs officers, and cranes. Merchant guilds operate here, and tolls fill the citys coffers.
Dockyard
A fortified dockyard with stone walls, dry docks for ship repair, and a dedicated staff handling both trade and naval logistics.
Grand Port Complex
The centerpiece of the city: a massive, stone-walled port with breakwaters, great warehouses, administrative quarters, and a customs house. Merchants from across the world gather here.
